note-a.text:
Idea: the brief is one floating Spotlight-style panel over a photo stage. Evolves the current site: warm stone ground, one selection blue, system type (zero font bytes), 44 px row rhythm.

Best at: familiarity and speed. Every option is a row you already know how to tap. Cheapest to build and fastest to load.

Worst at: brand. It borrows an operating-system look, so the wordmark does most of the brand work and the panel can feel like a tool rather than a company.

CHOSEN 9 Nov 2026.

note-b.text:
Idea: the brief is the headline. One large fill-in-the-blank sentence on warm paper; the blanks are the interface, options appear as chips under the blank you tapped. Editorial, type-led, one deep green.

Best at: brand and clarity. It is unmistakably Shoot, reads in two seconds, and makes Arabic look designed rather than translated (IBM Plex Sans + Plex Sans Arabic are one family).

Worst at: long option lists. Five chips fit; fifteen emirates or a date picker need a sheet, so step 2 of the flow has to change shape.

note-c.text:
Idea: the landing page is the start of the conversation. Shoot asks, you answer with chips, your brief forms as a message, and Send hands it to WhatsApp. Soft warm white, one teal, Rubik in both scripts.

Best at: matching the real journey. The client is going to WhatsApp anyway, so the page already behaves like it; first-timers on a phone need no instructions.

Worst at: premium. Chat bubbles read casual, and businesses booking corporate work may want something that feels more like a studio than a messenger.

s-note.text:
Screens use the Shoot Design System (installed on this canvas). Every label, option and price shown is placeholder data standing in for CMS content; no real creators, prices or photos exist yet, so photo slots show a warm illustrated scene tile as an honest stand-in, replaced by the CMS photo when one exists. Text in [SQUARE BRACKETS] is written by an editor in the CMS.

Sign-in is mobile number + OTP. Email/password exists only as an editor fallback, reached from the menu (06).

s-note-accounts.text:
Built from the live app (account home, /account/profile, /creators/{code}), same structure and copy, in the new design.

24 and 27 My account: who you are, then Up next (the one thing to do, as the Top Hit), then In your account with a status per place, briefs, Log out. The header's account icon opens it.

28 My profile: Draft status, Profile strength (one number and a bar), the peach "isn't complete yet" message with how many steps need attention, then the 7 steps as a sideways strip of tabs. Each tab: number (a tick when done), name, and a state line; required-and-missing reads in peach ("Needs languages"), recommended in grey ("Add a short bio"), done in blue. One step's panel at a time with Back / Next; missing fields are ringed in peach. Send for review stays off until nothing required is missing. Press Play to switch steps.

29: every step done, 100%, the steps as a list with ticks, Send for review on.

16 Public profile: Verified (only when identity is verified) with what it means, the deciding facts, Book with Omar, Actions, About, bio, Work.

30 Waiting for review: where the profile stands, and what to do meanwhile.

31 Availability: tap a day to block or free it; booked days are fixed. Press Play to try it.

32 Bookings: the request that needs an answer is the one primary action; the rest is a list.

s-note-flow.text:
Flow change (owner, 9 Nov): sign-in is no longer a gate. The client builds the brief (05), picks a creator (07), adds details (09), and only then gives their mobile number (10) and the code (11). The code signs them in, saves the booking and opens WhatsApp in one tap.

After that the same link shows the quotation to accept (12), the confirmed booking and how to pay (13), and the delivery to confirm (14). Payment is recorded by our team; nothing is paid on the site.

Screens 20 and 21 stay as the standalone sign-in for returning clients and creators (header account icon). Screen 09 no longer asks for a phone number.

The learning steps (02 to 04) show on the first visit only and can be skipped; each one is built from the real components, not an illustration.

s-note-landing.text:
Landing, full page (10 Nov, in motion). The hero is a golden-hour scene with a slow key light; the Brief Bar writes itself in and stays the one primary action. Below it:

1. What do you need shot?: occasion tiles that start a brief.
2. Meet the creators: a slowly moving strip of creator cards linking to profiles; "See all" opens the directory. It pauses on hover and keyboard focus. Its Pause control stops every loop on the page (the light, the strip, the sheen, the writing example, the small scenes), which is what WCAG 2.2.2 asks for; the 1440 landing (41) has the same control beside its creator columns. The writing example also ends the first time the bar is touched. Everything stands still under reduced motion. It shows only when there are enough real creators to fill it.
3. Shoot for a living?: the dark band for creators.
4. Ready when you are: back up to the brief.

How it works, Questions and the footer stay removed. Press Play to see it move.

s-note-step2.text:
07 Quick Match (9 Nov, revised): creators are a horizontal carousel. Each card is 296 px wide and snaps to the centre, so the next one peeks in at the edge; swiping changes the chosen creator (outlined in accent, its dot widens) and the Top Hit below follows: "Continue with Omar · AED 950". Tapping a card also chooses it and centres it. Press Play on this frame to swipe.

Card: work gallery (one large tile, two small; play mark on video), photo, name, code, emirates, years, specialties, languages, fixed price and what it includes. Below the rail: dots and "1 of 3" (announced to screen readers), the Top Hit, a link to the chosen creator's profile, and a "Let us pick" row.

No ratings, verified badges or review counts: none exist yet.

s-note-new.text:
Added 10 Nov: 19 screens, so every route in the app has a design. The canvas is now laid out in the order a person meets the screens, numbered 01 to 43.

New: 06 Menu · 08 No one free · 12 Quotation to accept · 14 Delivered · 17 Book this creator · 18 Work by specialty · 19 Hire page · 22 Wrong code · 23 Join as a creator · 30 Waiting for review · 31 Availability · 32 Booking requests · 33 Guides · 34 Guide article · 35 Editor-built page · 36 Terms · 38 Page removed · 39 Something went wrong · 40 Quotation expired.

Menu (06): with the footer gone from the landing, the menu is the one place for Creators, Guides, How it works, language, theme, Terms, Professional terms, Privacy and the editor sign-in. The header's menu button opens it.

How it works (35) is an editor-built page, not a landing section. It reuses the three learning steps and takes its questions from the CMS.

Each screen still has one solid blue action. Legal (36) has none: it is for reading.

Open for the owner: counts such as "12 pros" and "3 free" are placeholders and show only when real data exists.

s-note-motion.text:
Motion and graphics (10 Nov), on all 43 screens. Press Play on a board to see it.

Rise: content arrives in order.
Focus: photo slots sharpen in.
Glint: a sheen crosses the blue action once, 2.4 s after it arrives. Every 7 s on the landing only.
Roll: totals roll up.
Tick: confirmations draw themselves.
Key light: loops on the landing only. On the learning steps and the confirmed booking it settles once, inside 5 s. The splash plays once, in 2 s. Every other screen gets a still warm light in the corner.

Only the landing loops, and its Pause control stops all of it. Every other screen is still within 5 s, so a board plays its motion once after you press Play. All of it stands still under reduced motion. Scene tiles are stand-ins for photos, never invented work.
